sections.text:
يتكون نظام الاطفاء الذاتى بغاز 
 Co2 من عدد من الاسطوانات يوجد بداخلها غاز ثانى اكسيد 
 الكربون فى حالته السائلة تحت ضغط 80 بار تقريبا كما يتم وضع هذه الاسطوانات فى 
 مجموعات طبقا لكمية الغاز المطلوبة للاطفاء وتكون كل مجموعة من هذه المجموعات 
 مخصصة لاطفاء الحريق فى منطقة محددة تتناسب مع حجم الغاز داخل هذه الاسطوانات 
 ويوجد رشاشات لغاز الاطفاء ومكثفات لهب موزعة كما بالجدول التالى:-

وكل من مكتشف اللهب 
والحرارة لها خطين غير معتمدين على بعضهما ولكى يعمل نظام الحريق لا بد ان تاتى 
اشارة انذار بوجود حريق من احد مكتشفات الحريق على الخط الاول وقترنة بانذار على 
احد مكتشفات الحريق على الخط الثانى فان سولونيد تحرير الاوزان يتحرق فيعمل نظام 
الحريق وفى نفس الوقت تذهب اشارة الخروج الاضطرارى

يتم

sections_en.text: The CO2 automatic fire extinguishing system consists of a number of cylinders containing carbon dioxide gas in its liquid state at a pressure of approximately 80 bar. These cylinders are arranged in groups according to the quantity of gas required for extinguishing, and each group is dedicated to extinguishing a fire in a specific area commensurate with the volume of gas inside these cylinders. There are extinguishing gas sprinklers and flame detectors distributed as in the following table:-

Each of the flame and heat detectors has two independent lines, and for the fire system to operate, a fire alarm signal must come from one of the fire detectors on the first line together with an alarm from one of the fire detectors on the second line; then the weight-release solenoid moves and the fire system operates. At the same time, the emergency trip signal goes from the limit switch to the various components of the unit so that they stop, and the slow turning system operates to rotate the unit shaft.
When the system operates or is tested, the weight-release solenoid moves and the weight carrier arm drops down, and the weight-release box is reset to the operating position.

This document was prepared by Eng. Yousry Abdel Halim Abdel Latif and tested by Eng. Wasfy William Nashed - Senior Engineer, Occupational Safety and Health Department - and approved by Eng. Mohamed Mohamed El-Lawandy, General Manager. It was reviewed by Chemist Ahmed El-Sayed Ibrahim and Eng. Soliman Zaki Soliman, General Manager of Quality Assurance and Quality Control, and approved by Eng. Mohamed Mohamed Farag Anan - Head of the Damietta Power Generation Station Sector - and Eng. Mohamed Hussein Gomaa, Head of the Quality Assurance and Quality Control Sector at the East Delta Electricity Production Company.

rows: Open the work order from the Occupational Safety and Health Department
Open the weight-release box cover by pressing the cover lock push button (Push button lock)
Check that solenoid No. 4 is in the normal operating condition, i.e. the solenoid shaft is down
Turn both the safety catch No. 5 and the cam No. 6 together as far as possible clockwise so as to allow returning the cable clamping arm No. 7 to the operating position
The clamping arm No. 7 must be fixed on cam No. 6
Turn the safety catch No. 5 further and then fix it on the source No. 8 of weight-release arm No. 2
Push weight-release arm No. 2 down so that safety catch No. 5 is fixed on bumper 8, and thus mechanism No. 9 is in the tensioned condition and signal switch No. 13 is in the operating position
The upper ball of cable No. 10 must be placed in the ball socket of drop arm No. 11 and the cable must be checked to be fixed in its position
Hang the lower ball of cable No. 10 on the cable clamping arm holder No. 7
Fix weights No. 12 and weight-release arm No. 2
Close the weight-release box cover and secure its closing by means of the cover lock push button

Introduction
The CO2 automatic fire extinguishing system consists of a number of cylinders containing carbon dioxide gas in its liquid state at a pressure of approximately 80 bar. These cylinders are arranged in groups according to the quantity of gas required for extinguishing, and each group is dedicated to extinguishing a fire in a specific area commensurate with the volume of gas inside these cylinders. There are extinguishing gas sprinklers and flame detectors distributed as in the following table:-
Flame detector | Heat detector | Sprinklers | Number of cylinders | 
1 | 4 | 4 | 3 | Right combustion chamber
1 | 4 | 4 | 3 | Left combustion chamber
1 | 4 | 8 | 7 | Oil tank
Each of the flame and heat detectors has two independent lines, and for the fire system to operate, a fire alarm signal must come from one of the fire detectors on the first line together with an alarm from one of the fire detectors on the second line; then the weight-release solenoid moves and the fire system operates. At the same time, the emergency trip signal goes from the limit switch to the various components of the unit so that they stop, and the slow turning system operates to rotate the unit shaft.
When the system operates or is tested, the weight-release solenoid moves and the weight carrier arm drops down, and the weight-release box is reset to the operating position.
This document was prepared by Eng. Yousry Abdel Halim Abdel Latif and tested by Eng. Wasfy William Nashed - Senior Engineer, Occupational Safety and Health Department - and approved by Eng. Mohamed Mohamed El-Lawandy, General Manager. It was reviewed by Chemist Ahmed El-Sayed Ibrahim and Eng. Soliman Zaki Soliman, General Manager of Quality Assurance and Quality Control, and approved by Eng. Mohamed Mohamed Farag Anan - Head of the Damietta Power Generation Station Sector - and Eng. Mohamed Hussein Gomaa, Head of the Quality Assurance and Quality Control Sector at the East Delta Electricity Production Company.
Safety precautions
Open the work order from the Occupational Safety and Health Department | 
Wear personal protective equipment | 
Tools, instruments and equipment used
Pliers - Screwdriver set | 
Procedures to be carried out
Open the weight-release box cover by pressing the cover lock push button (Push button lock) | 1.
Check that solenoid No. 4 is in the normal operating condition, i.e. the solenoid shaft is down | 2.
Turn both the safety catch No. 5 and the cam No. 6 together as far as possible clockwise so as to allow returning the cable clamping arm No. 7 to the operating position | 3.
The clamping arm No. 7 must be fixed on cam No. 6 | 4.
Turn the safety catch No. 5 further and then fix it on the source No. 8 of weight-release arm No. 2 | 5.
Push weight-release arm No. 2 down so that safety catch No. 5 is fixed on bumper 8, and thus mechanism No. 9 is in the tensioned condition and signal switch No. 13 is in the operating position | 6.
The upper ball of cable No. 10 must be placed in the ball socket of drop arm No. 11 and the cable must be checked to be fixed in its position | 7.
Hang the lower ball of cable No. 10 on the cable clamping arm holder No. 7 | 8
Fix weights No. 12 and weight-release arm No. 2 | 9
Close the weight-release box cover and secure its closing by means of the cover lock push button | 10
